items.title: 1. Beach Morning Glory: what does the juice do when it touches your skin?
items.question:
The handling line says even picking a leaf "can affect me" when the juice from the broken part touches sensitive skin, especially under the fingernails. A fresh reader couldn't tell what that effect is.
(a) you feel the plant's effect, as you would from eating some (a trip starts to end); (b) a skin reaction, like a rash or a sting; or say it as you'd say it, and it goes into that sentence.
items.comment: touching the juice is relaxing, especially on sensitive skin, it absorbs almost as well as eating it. can put it under armpits for example to absorb well

items.title: 2. Beach Morning Glory: how big is the nibble for nausea?
items.question:
A fresh reader sitting with a friend couldn't judge "a tiny nibble" against the amount that ends a trip, and the paragraph says it takes only a little more than a nibble to end one, so a sitter could easily give too much.
How big is the nibble you'd give for nausea? Write it as you'd say it, as something a sitter can see (a part of a leaf, say), and it goes into that sentence. Or (a): leave it as "a tiny nibble".
items.comment: i'd try 10mg at a time for nausea of the extract paste, or 200mg leaf at a time (more if they don't mind reducing trip intensity)
